g.text: ❯ the API's rate limit is one shared window; make it a token bucket per key
● I'll replace the sliding window in limiter.py with a token bucket per
key, keeping the per_minute argument, and update the tests.
⎿ Updated limiter.py with 14 additions and 9 removals
● Done: each key now gets its own bucket of 10 that refills at per_minute.

Explain what this code does for a key that has been quiet for an hour.
It tops the bucket up for the hour that passed, at rate tokens a second, but never past burst, so the key gets its
Why time.monotonic() and a lock here, rather than time.time() and no lock?
Yes: the bucket refills for the time that passed and stops at burst, so an hour's quiet gives the key a full bucket
Why time.monotonic() and a lock here, rather than time.time() and no lock?
